title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1RC1LF_0RD1RD_1LE0RE_0LA0LB_---1LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1RC1LF_0RD1RD_1LE0RE_0LA0LB_---1LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The counter rounds and the E-chain that leads to the halting transition are proved in Lean for all lengths; the map from one right-end visit to the next is computed exactly when no timer runs out, and by examples when one does. No invariant that rules out the halting residue has been found.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 70,372 cells have been visited and 47,402 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.487). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).

claims.title: The counter rounds, for all run lengths
claims.text: Six rounds from one left-end visit to the next: the digit next to the left end goes 0→1→2→3, and 3 wraps to 0 with a carry into the next digit (0, 1 or 2), for all lengths of the runs of pairs and any tape to the right.

claims.title: The E-chain, the only way to halt
claims.text: With E on the last 1 of a run of c ones, each 111 becomes 110 in 3 steps; for c = 3k+3 the chain ends in E (then E0 → 0LA), for c = 3k+4 in B (then B0 → 1RC), for c = 3k+5 in F on a 0, which halts. So the machine halts exactly if E starts a chain on a run of length 2 mod 3.

claims.title: The right-end map, when no timer runs out
claims.text: With D on the last cell of 1^b<sub>0</sub> 0 … 0 1^b<sub>m−1</sub>, the next such visit has the blocks 6·4<sup>m</sup>+4, b<sub>0</sub>−d<sub>m−1</sub>, …, b<sub>m−1</sub>−d<sub>0</sub>, with d<sub>0</sub> = 9 and d<sub>i</sub> = 6·4<sup>i</sup>; checked on 60 random lists (m ≤ 5). When a block is smaller than its decrement the outcome is piecewise linear with period 12 (examples in the README).

claims.title: No halt to about 3.46·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: Continued from the right-end visit at step 8,352,788,565, the next one comes 26,203,435,131 steps later with blocks 223972, 42316, 24694, 2080, 21703, 2611, 1018, 373.

claims.title: The timers
claims.text: At the right-end visits (counter overflows) the last block loses 9 ones, the one before it 24, the one before that 96, the next about 384 (C simulation to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps, no halt).

claims.title: Twin: the same machine from state B
claims.text: Its twin 1RB1LF_0RC1RC_1LD0RD_0LE0LA_1RA0LB_---1LD halts from blank tape exactly when this machine halts from blank tape started in state B (step simulation with one transition replaced by three steps).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: the exhaustion cases of the right-end map are not in closed form, and no invariant excluding a chain on a run of length 2 mod 3 is known. Regular-language (CTL) searches over counter tokens failed.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a base-4 counter at the left end of its tape; each overflow sends the head to a stack of timers on the right, which run down at rates 9, 24, 96, … This page runs the real machine and explains the counter.

facts.text: Counter rounds and the E-chain, proved for all lengths.
1RB1LF_0RC1RC_1LD0RD_0LE0LA_1RA0LB_---1LD is this machine from state B.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.487). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).
After 109 steps the tape spans 70,372 cells (48,627 left of the start, 100 right), with a density of 1s of 0.674.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A base-4 counter
html: At each visit of the left end (state E) the tape begins (110)^n0 d0 (110)^n1 d1 …, each digit d one of 10, 1, 101, 11 (0 to 3). One round adds one:
The first run of pairs grows by one per round, so the left part grows like the square root of time; a carry out of digit i happens once every 4i+1 rounds.

sections.heading: Timers that run down
html: When the carry runs off the last digit, the head sweeps on to the right end, through long blocks of ones. At each such visit the last block loses 9 ones, the one before it 24, the next 96, the next about 384; when a timer is exhausted it is refilled from the blocks on its left. Overflows come exponentially rarely, so this side of the tape grows like a logarithm.

The machine halts exactly at the pattern F0: it happens when E reads a 1 whose left neighbour is a 1 with a 0 before it (`0 1 E>1` gives `E1 -> 0LB`, `B1 -> 1LF`, F on the 0); whether a refill ever produces it is the open question. Its twin 1RB1LF_0RC1RC_1LD0RD_0LE0LA_1RA0LB_---1LD behaves the same way with a different last timer.

sections.heading: From one overflow to the next
html: Halting needs one thing: state E starting the chain E1 → 0LB, B1 → 1LF, F1 → 1LE (each 111 becomes 110) on a run of ones of length 2 mod 3. Lengths 0 and 1 mod 3 end the chain harmlessly; all three cases are proved in Lean (lean/Chain.lean).

At a right-end visit the tape is just a list of blocks of ones. If none is too small, the next visit is exact: a new block 6·4m+4 appears on the left and the block j places from the right loses 9 (j = 0) or 6·4j. When a block runs out, the result depends on it modulo 12 and neighbouring blocks can merge; this part, and an invariant on block lists that keeps the bad residue away, are what a proof still needs.
Searches for a regular invariant (CTL) failed: forgetting the sizes of the blocks lets a tiny timer be eaten into a run of the bad length.

summary: A base-4 counter on the left; its overflows reach timer blocks on the right that lose 9, 24, 96, 384, … ones per visit (exact map when none runs out); halting needs an E-chain on a run of length 2 mod 3 (proved). Twin: 1RB1LF_0RC1RC_1LD0RD_0LE0LA_1RA0LB_---1LD, which is this machine from state B (proved).
